title: fix(spec): price cache.get at the catalog's input_cache_read rate, not the full input rate (the 1M context half landed in 0.1.3)
description:
# 🌙 dream: an openrouter tier atom declares the context its models actually serve

- kind: reseed
- owner: ehmpathy/rhachet-brains-openrouter
- caught: 2026-10-02

## .the cue that fired

the repo cut its default review brain over to `openrouter/deepseek/flash` (rhachet-brains-openrouter
0.1.1). at guard round i050, every review lane that held more than 96k tokens was refused before a
call was sent:

```
✋ ConstraintError: prompt exceeds 75% of context window
   ├─ 189.4% of 128000 tokens
```

the same lanes ran on `fireworks/*/flash` the round before, against a declared 1,048,576 tokens.

## .the gap, precisely

`dist/domain.operations/atom/BrainAtom.config.js` sets `gain.size.context.tokens: 128000` for both
the `pro` and `flash` tier estimates. `AtomSlug.unlisted.js` sets the same for any exact id.
`rhx review`'s 75% gate reads that figure, so a lane with more than 96k tokens is refused.

the file's own note says the figure leans low on purpose, and that "every tier model read on
2026-10-02 held 1M". openrouter's live catalog agrees: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` and
`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` both list `context_length: 1048576`.

the cache rate is a second, smaller gap of the same kind. the tier spec prices `cache.get` at the
full input rate ($0.30/M), but the catalog lists `input_cache_read` at about a fifth of `prompt`.
any spec-based estimate therefore models no cache discount at all.

## .the shape of the fix

1. set the tier estimate's context to the floor of what the tier's line serves today: 1,048,576
   for `deepseek/flash` and `deepseek/pro`, and likewise for each tier whose line holds 1M. the ci
   check that already compares rates to the cheapest live endpoint gains a twin: the declared
   context must sit at or below the picked model's `context_length`
2. better: if rhachet allows an async spec, or a spec refreshed at ask time, derive context and
   cache rate from the catalog pick, just as the model id is derived
3. then bump `rhachet-brains-openrouter` here and re-run the 5.1 guard on the openrouter lanes

## .the local stopgap, and when to remove it

`patches/rhachet-brains-openrouter@0.1.1.patch` (a `pnpm patch`) raises both tier estimates to
1,048,576 in this repo alone. once the upstream fix ships, bump the package and delete the patch
along with its `patchedDependencies` entry. pnpm refuses a patch whose version no longer matches,
so a bump left half done fails loud.

## .why it is not done in this round

it is not clean: the file lives in another repo's published package. a local override of a brain's
context window in this repo would defeat the safety the 75% gate exists for, and would hide the
defect from every other consumer.
